per_window.ps-ns: unresolved, abstract only. The C-terminal part of helix III is more flexible than its N-terminal part and R53 looks like a hinge in the free homeodomain at 286 K, 11.7 T (R15521-J3, r1).
per_window.us-ms: unresolved, abstract only. Slow conformational exchange at Y25 (entry 26) by both relaxation analyses (J1) and at K21, Q22, I38, H52 (entry 22, 23, 39, 53) by spectral density mapping only (J2); no dispersion, rate or population.
per_window.slower_than_ms: unresolved, abstract only. Amide H/D exchange rates point to a local fluctuation at N51-R53 (J5, r3).
per_window.undetermined: Helix III extension 51-59 less rigid with a kink at 51-53 (J4, r2); protease resistance of the C terminus at neutral pH (J6) and its increased accessibility after DNA binding (J7); DNA-bound human NKX2-1 crystal (J8). Not judged: r4 (database survey of other proteins), r5 (equilibrium thermal unfolding by CD/DSC at pH 5.0), r6 and r7 (3.5 ns MD of modelled DNA complexes, abstract only, no dynamics result).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Possibly, but only from an abstract: in the free rat TTF-1 homeodomain at 286 K (11.7 T) 15N relaxation analysis assigns slow conformational exchange to Y25 (entry Y26) by both model-free and spectral density mapping, and to K21, Q22, I38 and H52 by spectral density mapping only, with no dispersion, rate or population.
protein_summary.deposition_readback: Deposition-derived; same numbers RelaxDB labels were computed from; not literature confirmation. BMRB 15521 holds 500 MHz T1, T2 and NOE for 65 residues with metadata pH 4.3 and 286 K, the field and temperature of the abstract-only relaxation study; no source names the accession. R2/R1 above 8.08 flags K22, Q23 and I39 (author K21, Q22, I38), three of the four RSDM-only exchange residues. Y26 (author Y25) has the largest R2, 26.3 s-1 against about 12-14 s-1 in the helices, but NOE 0.53, so the screen calls it fast; H53 (author H52) has NOE 0.63. NOE below 0.65 marks R2-L8, H53, R54 and M57-Q68 plus L17, K25-L27, E31, M38 and Q45. Median R2/R1 over NOE >= 0.65 residues (7.2) gives about 9.5 ns by the rigid-rotor formula, near the abstract's 9.85-10.51 ns.
open_conflicts: C-terminal region: disordered or less rigid by NMR under acidic conditions (r2) versus protease-inaccessible at neutral pH (r9); the proteolysis abstract names the pH difference and the methods measure different things, so this is kept as a condition difference.
questions_for_gina: Is BMRB 15521 (500 MHz, 286 K, pH 4.3) the data set of the 2008 relaxation study, and can its full text be read so Y25 and the RSDM-only exchange residues can be judged above abstract level?
Should the deposited R2 of Y26 (26.3 s-1 with NOE 0.53) be read as exchange despite the low NOE, given that the abstract assigns slow exchange to Y25 by both methods?
protein_summary.buffer_note: Every rat TTF-1 homeodomain row except the human crystal is abstract-only, so no verdict above unresolved is possible. NMR on this domain was done under acidic conditions (pH 4.3 in the deposition), proteolysis at neutral pH and calorimetry at pH 5.0; the domain unfolds at 32 °C without salt (r5), so temperature and salt matter. R15521-r1 lists its conditions as not specified, yet the abstract gives 286 K and 11.7 T; the judgments use those values. Second read flagged no row.
